text:
Jordan: Heads up — AWS partner says they can start sending compact usage blobs hourly starting next week, but the payload schema is slightly different from our contract. Need quick alignment: can infra accept gzipped NDJSON within our 10m ingestion SLA? cc @Anya @Ravi
Anya: Do we have a strict 10m SLA on partner uploads? I thought ingestion window tolerance was 15m for marketplace channels.
Ravi: Current pipeline checkpoint expects hourly files with event timestamps and an idempotency_key. 10m vs 15m is ok from infra side, but we need to confirm how we backfill late files and whether we expect dedupe on our side.
Mei: We can accept gzipped ndjson. Just need the file name pattern and a header with partner_id and sequence_number. Also need a checksum header for quick integrity checks.
Luis: Partner asked if we can accept a single file containing multiple account namespaces (they include multiple customers in one blob). Is that allowed?
Tara: Billing prefers one namespace per file for traceability, but we can accept multi-namespace if they provide per-account line metadata: "account_id", "entitlement_snapshot_ts", "usage_units". We'll need explicit mapping to SKU.
Jordan: Good call. I'll ask them to include per-line sku_id and account_id. Also they asked about timezone: they will timestamp in UTC but the partner uses local midnight for daily aggregates — need to ensure our rollups align.
Anya: Ask them to always send event_ts in RFC3339 UTC. If they must include local_day, include local_tz too. We normalize to UTC for ledgering.
Ravi: Two other items: 1) idempotency_key must be stable per file (we use it to dedupe retries). 2) We need a small sample payload to validate ingestion mapping. Example we expect:
```json
{"account_id":"acct_123","sku_id":"redwood.small","event_ts":"2026-03-22T13:00:00Z","usage_units":120,"idempotency_key":"file-20260322-001"}
```
Mei: Also include a per-file manifest in headers: partner_id, file_seq, compressed:true, checksum:sha256. That lets the watcher skip partial files.
Luis: Partner asked about late deliveries and credits. If a file arrives >48h late we treat it as backfill, and finance may need manual review. Is that the current policy?
Tara: Yes — >48h late triggers finance review for crediting. We can automate flagging but not auto-crediting. Please surface late-file metrics to billing dashboard.
Jordan: OK. Proposed onboarding checklist for partner: 1) sample gzipped NDJSON file 2) schema mapping table (field -> Redwood field) 3) filename pattern + manifest headers 4) idempotency policy + retry cadence 5) test replay for 72h window 6) SLA agreement doc. Thoughts?
Anya: Add a test harness step: they should POST to a staging S3 bucket + send a signed webhook to our staging ingestion lambda so we can validate and emit sample ledger entries.
Ravi: We should include an explicit dedupe policy: we dedupe by (partner_id, file_seq, idempotency_key). If any line-level duplicate keys exist, we accept first-seen and log the duplicate. Add that to contract.
Mei: I'll prepare a small validation script we can share (python snippet) to check headers, checksum, and example mapping.
Jordan: Nice. Luis, can you confirm partner can emit per-line sku_id and include checksum? Also confirm they can run staging replay by Friday?
Luis: Pinged them — they confirmed gzipped ndjson + per-line sku_id doable, checksum yes. Staging replay by Friday is likely but they may need help with signing webhooks.
Jordan: Perfect. I'll draft the ingestion contract and SLA, include the dedupe policy and late-file playbook. I'll post the draft here when ready. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: ingestion-pipeline: new staging bucket created at s3://redwood-partner-staging/4167890123/ — notify when you upload test files.
Tara: Also request they include an "entitlement_snapshot_ts" per line so we can reconcile entitlements vs usage at ingest time. Saves a lot of back-and-forth.
Luis: Relay that to them now.
Anya: Sounds good. If Jordan posts the draft, I'll review and add billing acceptance criteria.
Jordan: Will do. Thanks everyone!
